newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: HORSE RACING-TIMARIDA KEEPS IRISH CHAMPION STAKES AT HOME.
newsitem.headline: HORSE RACING-TIMARIDA KEEPS IRISH CHAMPION STAKES AT HOME.

text.p: Timarida, trained in Ireland by John Oxx and ridden by Johnny Murtagh, landed her third successive group one race when she won the Irish Champion Stakes on Saturday.
Epsom Derby winner Shaamit, the 5-4 favourite, finished a disappointing fourth of the six runners.
Timarida, the 3-1 second favourite, successful in seven of her eight outings in 1995, is the first Irish-trained runner to keep the 10 furlong (2-km) race at home since 1986.
Held up behind the pacesetting Dance Design (9-2) until the field turned for home, Timarida was driven up the stands side by Murtagh at the furlong (200 metre) pole.

The Aga Khan's filly held on to win by one-and-a-half lengths from Dance Design, the mount of Michael Kinane, who had a neck to spare over English raider Glory Of Dancer (10-1), ridden by Frenchman Olivier Peslier.
Shaamit, partnered as at Epsom by Michael Hills, failed to get a clear run on the inside but was beaten on merit.
Newmarket trainer William Haggas said of Shaamit: "I won't know what went wrong until I get to watch the race again on video.

"There is no way I would blame jockey Michael Hills. This is only a small set-back. Shaamit is a good horse and we are likely to go for either the English Champion Stakes near our base at Newmarket or the Prix de l'Arc de Triomphe."
Hills felt Shaamit had been beaten because the pace set had been too slow, but he said: "We got absolutely no run."
Trainer Oxx said of the winner: "She is a terrific filly and has now won 10 of her 14 races. The standard she sets keeps going up all the time. Timarida is very consistent and is a great competitor."
Oxx said he would have to think about where the four-year- old will race next.
"The English Champion Stakes is the next obvious race for her but she might not like the straight course of Newmarket. She might prefer the more round-style courses of America." he said.
Last time out Timarida won a grade one fillies race at Arlington in the United States.
